detail: The hollis ledger lives on the customs counter. Hollis is customer — quartermaster of the asset trade, keeper of the counter's copy of the standard, signatory of the hollis ledger. A seal is not an entry: the clearance the customs gives is the trade's permission; the hollis ledger's entry is the world's adoption of the thing. The whole separation of customs from store is what keeps those two from merging again.
note: The hollis ledger is on the customs counter, but the seal never writes to it. Clearance is permission; entry is adoption.
